tests.title: The four server routes answer at the root whatever the mount point, and the mount point in use is reported
given: a service built with the default configuration
a service built with the mount point configured to /api/v2
tests.when: each of GET /healthz, /readyz, /version and /metrics is requested against each service
then: every route answers with a non-404 status on both services
GET /version reports mount_point /api/v1 on the default service
GET /version reports mount_point /api/v2 on the reconfigured service
tests.pseudocode: in the HTTP router's test file: for mp in ['/api/v1', '/api/v2']: app = build(mountPoint=mp); for p in ROOT_ROUTES: assert get(app, p).status != 404; assert get(app, '/version').json.mount_point == mp

tests.title: A path that matches no route is answered 404 in the error envelope
given: a service with the default mount point
tests.when: paths that match no route are requested: one under the mount point, one at the root, one deep under the mount point, and one that is a prefix of a server route
then: each answers 404
each body is {"error": {"code": 404, "message": <non-empty string>}}
no body carries an error_type key
tests.pseudocode: in the HTTP router's test file, table-driven over the four paths: r = get(app, path); assert r.status == 404 and r.json.error.code == 404 and r.json.error.message != '' and 'error_type' not in r.json.error

tests.title: A server route requested with a method other than GET is answered 405
given: a service with the default configuration
tests.when: each server route is requested with POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE
then: each answers 405
each body is the error envelope with code 405
the route's handler is not invoked
tests.pseudocode: in the HTTP router's test file, table over the four routes x four methods, with the handlers replaced by recording stubs: assert r.status == 405 and stub.calls == 0

tests.title: An error is rendered as the envelope, carrying error_type only when one was raised
given: the error renderer
tests.when: errors are rendered for a range of statuses, some raised with a machine-readable class and some without
then: every body is application/json carrying error.code equal to the status and a non-empty error.message
a body for an error raised with a class carries that class in error.error_type
a body for an error raised without a class has no error_type key at all, rather than the key with a null value
tests.pseudocode: in the error renderer's test file, table over (status, class|none): body = render(err); assert body.error.code == status; assert ('error_type' in body.error) == (class is not None); when present assert body.error.error_type == class

tests.title: An unexpected failure is answered 500 with a fixed message and the detail reaches only the log
given: a route whose handler raises an error carrying a distinctive secret string
a recording log sink
tests.when: that route is requested
then: the response is 500 with error.message exactly "internal server error"
the response body does not contain the distinctive string anywhere
the log sink received a record containing the distinctive string
tests.pseudocode: in the HTTP router's test file: app = build(logSink=rec); register('/boom', () => { throw Error('SENTINEL-9f3a') }); r = get(app, '/boom'); assert r.status == 500 and r.json.error.message == 'internal server error' and 'SENTINEL-9f3a' not in r.text; assert any('SENTINEL-9f3a' in x for x in rec.records)

tests.title: A request body over the limit is refused with 413 before the handler runs
given: a service with the default body limit
a service with the body limit configured to 1024 bytes
a recording handler on a POST route
tests.when: bodies at the limit, one byte over it, far over it, and empty are posted to each service
then: a body of exactly the limit is accepted and reaches the handler
a body one byte over the limit answers 413 in the error envelope
the handler is not invoked for any body over the limit
the default limit is 1048576 bytes
tests.pseudocode: in the HTTP router's test file, table over (limit, size, expectAccepted): app = build(maxBody=limit, handler=rec); r = post(app, '/t', 'x'*size); assert accepted ? (r.status != 413 and rec.calls == 1) : (r.status == 413 and rec.calls == 0)

tests.title: Timestamps are rendered as RFC 3339 UTC and parsed from any offset, and a malformed value is refused
given: the timestamp facility
tests.when: instants are rendered, and values are parsed: a Z value, a +02:00 value, a -08:00 value, one with fractional seconds, and the malformed values "2026-13-01T00:00:00Z", "not-a-time" and ""
then: every rendered value ends in Z and matches the RFC 3339 UTC form
each valid offset parses to the same instant as its UTC equivalent and renders with a Z offset
each malformed value is refused with a 400 in the error envelope whose message names the field
tests.pseudocode: in the timestamp facility's test file, two tables: render cases assert the regex; parse cases assert parse('2026-01-02T05:04:05+02:00') == parse('2026-01-02T03:04:05Z') and that malformed values produce a 400 naming the field

tests.title: The liveness probe answers ok without touching any store
given: a service whose relational store is a recording stub that fails on any call
tests.when: GET /healthz is requested
then: the response is 200 with body {"status": "ok"}
the store stub recorded no call
tests.pseudocode: in the server routes' test file: app = build(store=failing_recorder); r = get(app, '/healthz'); assert r.status == 200 and r.json == {'status': 'ok'}; assert store.calls == 0

tests.title: The readiness probe reflects whether the relational store really answers
given: the service wired to a real relational store through its platform interface
tests.when: GET /readyz is requested while the store answers, and again after the store has been made unreachable
then: the first answers 200 with body {"status": "ready"}
the second answers 503 with the error envelope and error.code 503
the probe recovers to 200 once the store answers again
tests.pseudocode: in the server routes' integration test file, against the non-Cloudflare store implementation: assert get('/readyz').status == 200; store.stop(); assert get('/readyz').status == 503; store.start(); assert get('/readyz').status == 200

tests.title: The server routes need no credential
given: a service with the default configuration
tests.when: each of the four server routes is requested with no Authorization header, and with a malformed one
then: no response is 401 on any of the eight requests
tests.pseudocode: in the server routes' test file, table over the four routes x (no header, 'Bearer nonsense'): assert get(app, route, headers).status != 401

tests.title: The version route reports the build and the runtime under truthful keys
given: a service built with a build time and a commit
a service built with neither
tests.when: GET /version is requested against each
then: the body's keys are exactly build_time, commit, mount_point and runtime_version
there is no go_version key
runtime_version is a non-empty string and mount_point is the configured mount point
the service built with neither reports "" for build_time and commit and still answers 200
the response carries a Cache-Control header permitting public caching
tests.pseudocode: in the server routes' test file: r = get(app, '/version'); assert set(r.json.keys()) == {'build_time','commit','mount_point','runtime_version'}; assert r.json.runtime_version != ''; assert 'public' in r.headers['Cache-Control']

tests.title: The metrics route exposes every documented metric in Prometheus text format
given: a freshly started service that has answered no request
tests.when: GET /metrics is requested and the body is parsed as Prometheus text exposition
then: the response is 200 with Content-Type "text/plain; version=0.0.4"
the body parses as Prometheus text exposition
every metric name the API reference's metrics table lists is present with the type that table gives it and with exactly its label names
every metric for which the service has no source yet is present with the value 0
tests.pseudocode: in the metrics test file: r = get(app, '/metrics'); fams = parse_prometheus(r.text); for name, typ, labels in API_METRICS_TABLE: assert fams[name].type == typ and fams[name].label_names == labels; for name in SOURCELESS: assert value(fams[name]) == 0

tests.title: An answered request is counted and timed under its method, route template and status
given: the service with its real metrics sink, having answered no request
tests.when: one request is made to a matched route and the metrics are read
then: afhub_http_requests_total for that method, route template and status reads 1
afhub_http_request_duration_seconds for that method and route template has exactly one observation
the histogram's bucket boundaries are the ones the API reference lists
tests.pseudocode: in the metrics integration test file: get(app, '/healthz'); fams = parse_prometheus(get(app, '/metrics').text); assert sample(fams, 'afhub_http_requests_total', {'method':'GET','path':'/healthz','status':'200'}) == 1; assert histogram_count(fams, 'afhub_http_request_duration_seconds', {'method':'GET','path':'/healthz'}) == 1

tests.title: Unmatched paths cannot grow the metric label set
given: a freshly started service
tests.when: 50 requests are made to 50 distinct paths that match no route, and the metrics are read
then: the path label of afhub_http_requests_total takes exactly one value for those 50 requests
that one value is not any of the 50 requested URIs
the counter for that single label set reads 50
tests.pseudocode: in the metrics test file: for i in range(50): get(app, f'/api/v1/nope-{i}'); labels = {s.labels['path'] for s in samples(fams, 'afhub_http_requests_total') if s.labels['status'] == '404'}; assert len(labels) == 1

tests.title: Every platform interface satisfies one contract suite with both of its implementations
given: the shared contract suite of each platform interface this package defines: the relational store, the clock, the configuration source and the metrics sink
tests.when: the contract suite of each interface is run against its Cloudflare implementation and against its non-Cloudflare implementation
then: every case passes against both implementations
the suite is the same code in both runs, parameterised only by which implementation it is given
a case that passes against one implementation and fails against the other is reported as a failure, not a skip
tests.pseudocode: in each interface's contract test file: for impl in [cloudflareImpl(), localImpl()]: runContractSuite(impl) — one suite definition, two parameterised runs

tests.title: The service answers identically whichever implementation of the platform interfaces it is given
given: the service wired in process to the Cloudflare implementations
the service wired in process to the non-Cloudflare implementations
tests.when: the four server routes are requested against each wiring, and the readiness probe is requested again after each wiring's relational store has been made unreachable
then: each route answers with the same status under both wirings
each response body carries the same keys under both wirings, differing only in the values of build_time, commit and the measured metric samples
the readiness probe answers 503 in the error envelope under both wirings once the store is unreachable
tests.pseudocode: in the platform parity integration test file: for wiring in [cloudflareWiring(), localWiring()]: app = build(wiring); record status and body keys for each of ROOT_ROUTES; wiring.store.stop(); record get('/readyz'). Then assert the two recordings are equal field for field except build_time, commit and metric values.

tests.title: The second target serves the same four routes on one host with no Cloudflare account
given: the second target started as its single artefact on one host, with its own relational store and no network access to Cloudflare
tests.when: the four server routes are requested against it, its relational store is then stopped, and the readiness probe is requested again
then: each route answers with the same status and the same body keys as the Cloudflare deployment, differing only in build_time, commit and measured metric values
after the store is stopped the readiness probe answers 503 in the error envelope
the run completes with no Cloudflare credential present in the environment
tests.pseudocode: in the second target's smoke test file: proc = start_local_target(); for p in ROOT_ROUTES: assert shape_of(get(proc.url + p)) == shape_of(reference_response(p)); proc.store.stop(); assert get(proc.url + '/readyz').status == 503

tests.title: An operator probes a real Cloudflare deployment and reads its build information
given: the service deployed to Cloudflare from the checked-in configuration, with a real relational store
tests.when: GET /healthz, GET /readyz and GET /version are requested in turn against the deployment's base URL
then: the liveness probe answers 200 with {"status": "ok"}
the readiness probe answers 200 with {"status": "ready"}, having queried the real store
the version route reports the build time, commit, mount point and runtime version of that deployment
tests.pseudocode: in the deployment smoke test file, skipping with a named reason when no deployment URL is configured: assert get(base + '/healthz').json == {'status':'ok'}; assert get(base + '/readyz').json == {'status':'ready'}; assert get(base + '/version').json.runtime_version != ''

tests.title: A missed route is answered in the envelope and shows up in the scraped metrics
given: a running deployment that has answered no request
tests.when: an API client requests a path under the mount point that matches no route, and a scraper then reads GET /metrics
then: the client receives 404 with the error envelope
the scraped exposition counts that request in afhub_http_requests_total with status 404 and its latency observed
the path label of that sample is the fixed unmatched-route value, not the requested URI
tests.pseudocode: in the deployment smoke test file: get(base + '/api/v1/no-such-thing'); fams = parse_prometheus(get(base + '/metrics').text); s = sample(fams, 'afhub_http_requests_total', status='404'); assert s.value >= 1 and s.labels['path'] != '/api/v1/no-such-thing'

tests.title: The harness reports every check's outcome and sets its exit code from the failures
given: the harness configured with a passing check, a failing check and a skipping check, against a stub deployment
tests.when: the harness is run against the stub deployment's base URL, and then run again with the failing check removed
then: the report names all three checks, each with outcome pass, fail or skip
the first run exits non-zero because a check failed
the second run exits 0 although a check was skipped
tests.pseudocode: in the harness test file: r = run_harness(baseURL=stub.url, checks=[ok, bad, skipped]); assert r.exit != 0 and {c.name: c.outcome for c in r.report} == {'ok':'pass','bad':'fail','skipped':'skip'}; r2 = run_harness(checks=[ok, skipped]); assert r2.exit == 0

tests.title: The harness builds afc from the pinned hub commit
given: the Go toolchain and a network available
the pinned commit of github.com/agent-fox-dev/hub recorded in the repository
tests.when: the harness prepares a check that needs afc
then: an afc binary is built and is executable
the harness reports the commit it built from
the reported commit is the one pinned in the repository, not a branch tip
tests.pseudocode: in the harness test file, skipping with a named reason when Go or the network is absent: b = harness.prepare_afc(); assert is_executable(b.path) and b.commit == read_pin()

tests.title: A check whose dependency is missing is skipped with a named reason and does not change the outcome
given: the harness with checks declaring a missing binary, an unreachable network and an absent deployment
tests.when: the harness is run with none of those dependencies available, alongside one passing check
then: each dependent check has outcome skip
each skip message names the dependency that was missing
the exit code is the same as a run defined with the passing check alone
tests.pseudocode: in the harness test file, table over the three missing-dependency kinds: r = run_harness(checks=[ok, dependent]); assert outcome(dependent) == 'skip' and dependency_name in message(dependent) and r.exit == run_harness(checks=[ok]).exit

tests.title: The fast check passes offline with no deployment
given: a checkout with dependencies installed, no network access and no deployment configured
tests.when: the project's fast check command is run
then: it exits 0
its output reports the conformance checks as skipped rather than failed
no check attempts a network call
tests.pseudocode: in the build gate's test file: r = run('make check', env=no_network, deployment=None); assert r.exit == 0 and 'skip' in r.output.lower()
